title: Quebec Court Fines Man for AI-Generated Fabricated Legal Documents
summary: A man in Quebec submitted AI-generated fabricated legal documents as part of his legal defense in court. A Quebec judge fined the man $5,000 for improper use of artificial intelligence in court.

title: Ukraine Ministry of Defence approves Zmiy Droid 12.7 combat robot for deployment
summary: The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine approved the Zmiy Droid 12.7, a ground-based combat robot for deployment by the Armed Forces of Ukraine. The system is manufactured by two Ukrainian defense contractors and is designed to perform military tasks in high-intensity combat conditions. The robot is built on the Zmiy platform and equipped with the Wolly remote-controlled combat module armed with a 12.7mm machine gun. The combat module is fitted with AI systems capable of automatically acquiring and tracking targets in autonomous mode. Reported impact The Ministry stated that such armed ground robots have performed well in modern warfare conditions. Examples cited include documented strikes against Russian MT-LB vehicles using a related Droid TW 12.7 system, and sustained defensive fire missions lasting 45 consecutive days. Index analysis The system operates with an autonomous targeting capability that reduces decision-making time in combat. The control module enables simultaneous operation of the platform and combat module by a single operator. Governance controls The Ministry of Defence approved the system for operational use in the Armed Forces of Ukraine. The robot was developed by engineers with significant experience manufacturing and deploying ground platforms in high-intensity warfare.
place: Armed Forces of Ukraine HQ: Kyiv

title: Ukrainian forces shoot down Russian AI-powered Kamikaze drone Klin
summary: Fighters of the 118th Separate Mechanized Brigade of the Ukrainian Armed Forces shot down a Russian AI-powered kamikaze drone called 'Klin' on the Orikhovskyi direction using a Ukrainian 'General Chereshnya AIR' interceptor drone. This was the first recorded destruction of the Klin drone, which Russia presented only four months prior to the incident. The Klin is a 'Shahed-like' unmanned aerial vehicle equipped with an artificial intelligence system for guidance. Reported impact The Klin drone features autonomous target detection and attack capability at ranges up to 120 km and can operate as an 'aerial minefield' while loitering for approximately 80 minutes. It has a takeoff weight of 13.5 kg, flight speed between 108–300 km/h, fuselage length of 1.6 m, wing span of 1.9 m, maximum flight altitude up to 2 km, and a warhead weight of 5 kg.

title: German Cybersecurity Agency Warns of AI-Driven Vulnerability Discovery Risks
summary: Anthropic developed an AI model called Claude Mythos designed to discover hidden software vulnerabilities. The company announced it had found thousands of serious vulnerabilities using the tool, including in widely-used operating systems and web browsers. The German Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) warned that such AI-driven vulnerability discovery could have significant impacts on the cybersecurity threat landscape. BSI President Claudia Plattner stated the agency had not tested the tool but gained insight into its functioning through personal discussions with Anthropic developers. Reported impact The BSI warned that with rapid progress in artificial intelligence, such capabilities could soon be available to online attackers. The agency expects this technology could shift attack vectors and trigger a paradigm change in the cyberthreat landscape. The BSI cautioned that if the trend continues logically, there could be no unknown classic software vulnerabilities in the medium term, which would require a fundamental shift in cybersecurity approaches. The agency raised questions about how long such powerful tools will remain available on the open market and noted implications for national and European security. Governance controls Anthropic announced plans to provide access to Claude Mythos to select cooperating corporations including Apple, Amazon and Microsoft so they can find security gaps in their software. The company stated it does not plan to make Mythos publicly available. Other cooperation partners named included the Linux Foundation, cybersecurity firms Crowdstrike and Palo Alto Networks, and network specialist Cisco.
place: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik HQ: Bonn

title: AI-Generated Fake Video Spreads Disinformation About Ukrainian Gas Stations
summary: A video purporting to show a destroyed gas station in Kremenchuk, Poltava region circulated online, featuring what appeared to be a Ukrainian military officer stating that the station was attacked by small drones rather than Russian missiles, accusing the Ukrainian government of inaction, and predicting similar attacks on Kyiv. The Centre for Countering Disinformation confirmed the video was entirely generated using artificial intelligence. The video first appeared on an anonymous TikTok account, then was amplified by Russian Telegram channels. Reported impact The Centre noted that the video was part of a Russian disinformation campaign aimed at exaggerating the consequences of attacks on Ukrainian fuel infrastructure, creating an illusion of a major crisis, sowing fear among Ukrainians, and demoralizing society. Index analysis Signs of AI technology use indicated the recording was not genuine and could not be considered evidence of the events described in it.

title: Carlsen Verlag sues OpenAI for copyright infringement of "Das NEINhorn"
summary: Carlsen Verlag filed a lawsuit against OpenAI's Irish subsidiary, alleging that ChatGPT reproduces copyrighted content from the children's book series "Das NEINhorn" by Marc-Uwe Kling and Astrid Henn, first published in 2019. According to Carlsen, simple prompts in ChatGPT generate stories that closely match the original work's creative elements, with illustrations barely distinguishable from originals. ChatGPT also reportedly generates complete print templates including cover design, impressum, false order numbers, and publisher logos. Reported impact Carlsen alleges the originalworks' detailed reproduction indicates they were unlawfully used to train OpenAI's language and image models through memorization. Index analysis Author Marc-Uwe Kling stated that individuals face penalties for downloading a single film, book, or audiobook illegally, yet questioned why OpenAI can copy all art and culture worldwide without consequence.

title: Argentine media group Perfil sues OpenAI and Microsoft over unauthorized content use
summary: Editorial Perfil presented a lawsuit in Argentine federal court against OpenAI, Microsoft Corporation, and Microsoft de Argentina, alleging the companies used Perfil's journalistic content without authorization to train and commercially exploit AI systems. Perfil claims its content was downloaded from the internet, stored, and used to train AI models, including material protected by copyright and behind paywalls. The lawsuit alleges the content was used as 'free raw material' to generate chatbot responses and commercial products. Reported impact Perfil alleges that OpenAI and Microsoft obtained economic benefits by using Perfil's original, verified, and edited journalistic content without permission or compensation. Index analysis The lawsuit alleges intellectual property infringement and unfair competition, claiming the technology companies' concentration of power over user flows and information distribution on the internet enabled the misuse of content.

title: Sony and Warner Sue Anthropic Over Unauthorized Training on Copyrighted Music
summary: Sony Music and Warner Music filed a lawsuit against Anthropic, alleging the company illegally trained its AI models on tens of thousands of copyrighted music works. According to the 48-page complaint, Anthropic conducted a campaign of illegal torrent downloads, scraping, and downloading of protected works at massive scale to develop and profit from its Claude AI models. Reported impact The music publishers are seeking hundreds of thousands of dollars in compensation for each work they claim was infringed. Anthropic previously settled a related intellectual property case in September 2025 for $1.5 billion with authors and publishers.

title: Mexico's Women's Ministry Condemns Grok for Generating Non-Consensual Sexual Images
summary: Users have recently employed X's platform to generate semi-nude or sexually explicit images using AI and subsequently distribute them without the consent of the women depicted. Grok, X's AI chatbot, has facilitated the manipulation and dissemination of explicit images without victims' consent. Reported impact The conduct constitutes a violation of intimacy and a form of sexual violence against women. Mexico's Secretary of Women stated that such conduct is typified under the Ley Olimpia, which sanctions the production and dissemination of real or simulated intimate content that violates the integrity of women. Index analysis Mexico's Secretaría de las Mujeres stated that AI tools such as Grok lack sufficient security filters to prevent digital sexual violence. The Secretary of Women noted that X has no offices in Mexico, which creates difficulties in establishing meetings to address the issue, though the absence of local headquarters does not exempt technology companies from their ethical and legal responsibility. Governance controls The Secretaría de las Mujeres announced it has had contacts with the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones to seek to ensure that the digital environment does not become an extension of gender-based violence or a refuge for sexual harassment.
place: Secretaría de las Mujeres HQ: Mexico City

title: Delia's "Analog" music video cloned and altered with AI without consent
summary: Artist Delia Matache released a symphonic version of her song "Analog" performed with the Bucharest Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Andrei Tudor. Footage from the official music video was subsequently taken and used in another online video where the audio was replaced with a song generated by artificial intelligence and performed by a virtual character, and this modified video was published on social media. Reported impact Delia Matache stated the situation violates copyright and the use of creators' content without permission, saying "Aia e munca noastră" (that is our work). Conductor Andrei Tudor stated he never consented to the use of his name, image, or supposed contributions to the production, and raised concerns about respect for artists' rights and the use of identity without consent. Index analysis Delia questioned why footage from her video was extracted and reused: "Generează ce vrei, dar de why iei videoclipurile oamenilor?" (Generate what you want, but why do you take people's videos?). Andrei Tudor noted that the material appeared to be generated entirely with artificial intelligence, and expressed concern about who created and decided to associate his name and image with the content.

title: California fails to regulate automated license plate readers for fifth consecutive year
summary: California lawmakers failed to enact regulations on automated license plate readers (ALPR) for the fifth consecutive year. Senate Bill 1013 would have strengthened privacy protections on how license plate data is collected and shared, but was blocked in the Assembly on the final day of the legislative session before it could receive a floor vote. The bill would have guarded against misuse of ALPR by law enforcement, required privacy and cybersecurity training, and called for random audits by the California Attorney General's Office. Law enforcement agencies opposed the measure, arguing that the restrictions could limit use of historical license plate data in criminal investigations and missing-person cases. Reported impact Privacy advocates have raised concerns about misuse of license plate reader data, including improper data sharing, surveillance, and inaccurate alerts. More than 200 cities or law enforcement agencies ended license plate reader contracts in August 2026, the largest number in any month since 2021. One Bay Area privacy advocate was held at gunpoint by sheriff's deputies after a license plate reader incorrectly identified his vehicle as stolen. More than 230 California police and sheriff's departments currently use automated license plate readers. Index analysis The repeated failure to pass regulations reflects a governance gap regarding the use and oversight of AI-powered surveillance technology by law enforcement. The blocking of bipartisan legislation indicates the influence of law enforcement opposition to data restrictions despite documented misuse. Governance controls Law enforcement agencies in Los Angeles, Redwood City, El Cerrito and Campbell have ended contracts with Flock Safety in recent weeks amid growing privacy concerns. A similar bill passed in the previous legislative session but was vetoed by Governor Gavin Newsom.

title: Russia uses AI to amplify disinformation network against US
summary: Russia has escalated information attacks against the United States using artificial intelligence and a disinformation ecosystem, according to the Centre for Countering Disinformation at Ukraine's Council of National Security and Defence, citing analysis from NewsGuard. Russia has built a network of disinformation platforms known as Pravda, which includes over 150 websites across 49 countries that distributed more than 3.6 million materials containing Kremlin narratives in one year. The disinformation resources intentionally 'contaminate' search engines and AI models with false materials, causing AI algorithms to reproduce Kremlin messages and mislead users. Reported impact The network systematically attacks American media outlets by labeling them as 'fake' or 'propaganda'. Russia is attempting to attack democratic societies from within by undermining citizens' trust in their own governments through AI-powered disinformation and deepfakes. Index analysis AI models trained on or accessing poisoned data sources are compromised in their ability to provide accurate information, effectively weaponizing the systems against information integrity.

title: AI-Generated Deepfake Videos Spread Disinformation About Ukrainian Military Surrender
summary: AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting Ukrainian military forces surrendering near Pokrovsk, Donetsk region were disseminated on TikTok in a coordinated campaign. The videos, bearing captions in multiple foreign languages, originated from coordinated networks of accounts identified as designed to spread Kremlin narratives to international audiences. Reported impact The campaign aimed to convince international users that Ukraine was losing the war and military aid was futile, while demoralizing Ukrainian citizens by creating a sense of catastrophic military collapse. Ukraine's military reported continued intense fighting in Pokrovsk as of November 4, with defences holding against Russian assault. Index analysis The Disinformation Resistance Center identified the campaign as an information component of Russian military operations designed to shape international perception and domestic morale.

title: AI-generated deepfake videos spread on TikTok in Russian disinformation campaign targeting Ukraine
summary: Videos circulating on TikTok reportedly showed street interviews with ordinary Ukrainians discussing war, mobilization, and peace negotiations. According to Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation, all videos were entirely AI-generated and shared a uniform visual style. Video subjects expressed exclusively pessimistic messages: opposing mobilization, calling the war 'senseless,' blaming authorities for 'sabotaging peace,' and promoting the claim that reclaiming occupied territories is 'unnecessary.' Verification through deepfake detection services confirmed the videos were AI-generated. Reported impact The Center for Countering Disinformation stated the videos aimed to demoralize Ukrainian society and reduce resistance by promoting a narrative of 'peace at any price,' with the goal of imposing feelings of despair and hopelessness on Ukrainians. The Center described these videos as part of a new wave of information-psychological operations intended to undermine mobilization efforts in Ukraine. Index analysis The uniform visual style and consistently pessimistic messaging across videos suggests coordinated production rather than organic user-generated content. Governance controls Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation identified and publicly warned about the campaign, calling on citizens to be cautious and rely only on verified sources of information.

title: Criminal rings use AI to create fake investment realities in "Truman Show Scam"
summary: Criminal rings use an AI-powered system called OPCOPRO, known as the 'Truman Show Scam', to conduct sophisticated investment fraud. According to research by Check Point Software Technologies Ltd., the scheme involves creating entirely synthetic, AI-generated realities around victims. The fraud operates in four stages: initial contact via SMS or advertisements mimicking legitimate financial institutions, luring victims into WhatsApp or Telegram groups; creating fake investment communities with AI-generated 'experts' and members who simulate active trading environments with professional market commentary and staged daily gains; directing victims to download the official OPCOPRO application from legitimate app stores, which displays fake balances generated by the server despite containing innocuous code; and a final extraction phase where victims are pressured to deposit further funds. The scheme combines AI-generated digital personas, fabricated investment communities, mobile applications deployed as WebView shells in official app stores, and staged media presence to create the illusion of a legitimate institutional investment program. Reported impact Victims are not simply sent misleading messages but instead enter a staged world where every expert, chart, and 'profit' is fake. The continuous positive reinforcement and absence of disagreement within the synthetic communities create strong social proof that manipulates victims into believing in the fraudulent scheme. Index analysis The scam represents an evolution of cybercrime from isolated attacks to industrialized manipulation systems. The use of AI to generate synthetic personas and fake trading environments at scale demonstrates how generative technologies enable sophisticated social engineering that bypasses traditional skepticism.

title: AI deepfakes and harassment campaigns target Nigerian women, report warns
summary: Gatefield, a Sub-Saharan African public strategy and media group, released an analysis stating that generative AI is rapidly amplifying gender-based online abuse in Nigeria, with up to 70 million women and girls at risk of exposure by 2030, including 30 million likely to be directly targeted through deepfakes, impersonation and coordinated harassment campaigns. Based on Nigeria's projected 200 million internet users by 2030, the report estimates that nearly half of women online could be exposed to AI-facilitated harm. Platforms like X and Grok reportedly facilitated abuse through functionless content generation, delayed moderation, and opaque policies, described as unsafe product design. Reported impact According to Gatefield's 2025 report, nearly half of Nigerian internet users experience online harm, with women comprising 58% of victims. Research on Nigerian women targeted with non-consensual image sharing found that nearly 90% experienced depression or suicidal thoughts, with 11 out of 27 considering suicide and one attempting it. Index analysis AI-facilitated abuse constitutes structurally violent digital harm, systematically targeting women while exploiting both human and technological vulnerabilities. The report notes that Nigeria currently lacks AI-specific legislation, forensic capacity, and platform accountability frameworks. Governance controls Gatefield called for the introduction of AI-facilitated violence guidelines to define and address AI-generated cyber violence, including impersonation and political and social disinformation, and for coverage of AI-generated images, video, audio, and text that mislead, manipulate, or impersonate individuals.

title: Instagram Algorithm Allegedly Suppresses Jharkhand Student Protest Visibility
summary: Student protests took place at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and in Ranchi, Jharkhand, both concerning education and irregularities in competitive examinations. Data analysis collaboration between NDTV and DataBeings examined Instagram posts, accounts, reach, engagement and reel performance related to both protests. An analysis found a substantial difference in the scale of amplification between the two protests on Instagram. Posts about the Jantar Mantar protest in Delhi garnered millions of views, while posts about the similar protest in Ranchi received significantly fewer views despite featuring similar visual elements including large crowds, young protesters, clashes with police, tear gas, lathi charges and water cannons. Reported impact The contrasting social media visibility of the two protests raised questions about how Instagram determines which events receive widespread attention and which remain confined to smaller audiences. The disparity prompted concerns about whether the platform's algorithm contributed to boosting content related to Jantar Mantar protests while allegedly suppressing those against it. Index analysis Meta has acknowledged that money has been charged for boosting certain types of content on Instagram. The government of India is engaging with Meta over Instagram algorithm functioning, with Electronics and IT Secretary S Krishnan requesting detailed information from Meta to examine whether the significant difference in views is due to algorithmic manipulation. Social media platforms generally respond to such discrepancies by stating that posts about events that receive more audience tend to receive higher views. The analysis carried caveats noting that the two protests took place in different locations and at different stages. Governance controls The government of India is keeping an eye on the algorithm and examining the difference in views received between the Jantar Mantar and Ranchi protests. The government requested detailed information from Meta to determine whether algorithmic manipulation occurred.

title: FTC and States Settle Antitrust Case Against Corteva Over Pesticide Loyalty Program
summary: The FTC and state attorneys general reached a settlement agreement with Corteva Inc. over antitrust allegations brought in 2022. The lawsuit alleged that Corteva implemented a post-patent loyalty program that paid distributors to block competitors from selling cheaper generic pesticide products to farmers. Under the settlement terms, Corteva will dismantle its existing pesticides loyalty program and is prohibited for 10 years from conditioning payments or benefits to distributors on purchasing a high share of Corteva pesticide active ingredients or limiting purchases of generic equivalents. Reported impact The settlement is intended to lower pesticide prices for American farmers by ensuring greater access to lower-cost generic pesticide products. According to the complaint, Corteva's conduct allowed the company to maintain elevated prices, forcing farmers to spend millions of dollars more for essential crop protection products. Governance controls The settlement resolves claims against Corteva through a stipulated order lasting 10 years, which prohibits the company from using loyalty program practices to limit competition from generic pesticide manufacturers after patent expiration.
place: Federal Trade Commission HQ: Federal Trade Commission Building

title: AI-generated fake images of Celebrity lead to criminal charges in South Korea
summary: AI-generated synthetic images depicting South Korean celebrity Im Yuna as pregnant were created and spread on social media and online communities in June 2026 and again in September 2026. The images showed her face digitally combined with a pregnant body, sometimes accompanied by a man, without her consent. Reported impact SM Entertainment stated that the synthetic images and associated false claims caused harm to the artist's rights and reputation. The company indicated the images violated portrait rights and constituted defamation and illegal deepfake creation under South Korean law. Governance controls SM Entertainment established a reporting platform called 'KWANGYA 119' to collect complaints from fans and conduct ongoing monitoring of illegal content. The company stated it would pursue criminal charges without settlement or leniency, and warned that creating, sharing, or reposting the images could violate South Korean laws on defamation, portrait rights, and deepfake creation.

title: AI Chatbots Amplify Misinformation from Partisan "Pink Slime" News Sites
summary: NewsGuard tested seven major AI chatbots on questions about candidates and issues. Of 168 responses, 48.2% cited partisan "pink slime" websites alongside other sources, and 7.7% cited only pink slime websites, which disguise themselves as independent local news but are funded by political groups. ChatGPT cited pink slime websites in 70.8% of responses; Copilot and Perplexity each at 54.2%; Claude at 50%; others between 29.2% and 41.7%. In the 168 responses tested, only once did an AI system identify these websites as having partisan alignment. Pink slime websites present themselves as regular news media but are actually funded by groups with political or ideological purposes and do not disclose their funding sources or political views to readers. Reported impact NewsGuard found 1,179 pink slime websites in total, with 21 created this year, exceeding the 937 daily newspapers still operating in the United States according to Northwestern University's Local News Initiative. These websites confuse readers who may believe they are independent local media, thereby weakening trust between journalists and readers across the political spectrum. Experts warn the phenomenon may further erode public trust in traditional media. Index analysis AI chatbots are amplifying partisan content by citing pink slime websites as sources without consistently disclosing their political alignment, potentially increasing their reach and influence during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. The right-wing One Nation and left-wing American Independent networks spent at least $801,500 on Facebook and Instagram ads in the first eight months of 2026 to promote their articles, and increased online reach may further influence chatbot responses. Governance controls Microsoft's Copilot statement said the system responds based on high-quality search results and encourages users to review sources to verify accuracy. Six other tested AI companies did not respond to requests for comment.

title: Finland's Parliamentary Ombudsman Investigates AI Replacing Municipal Leadership
summary: Humppila municipality in Central Finland eliminated the administrative director and technical director positions and replaced their functions with AI systems. The municipal council approved the move following a proposal from new municipal manager Minna Ylikännö, with the stated goal of achieving 150,000 euros in budget savings. The AI system was deployed to draft administrative decisions, public procurement documents, and administrative regulations. Ylikännö reported using AI to complete administrative rule revisions in one day. Reported impact The Parliamentary Ombudsman's office opened an investigation to examine the lawfulness and governance implications of using AI for municipal government functions. The investigation examined what tasks were assigned to AI, how decision-making legality and proper procedures are ensured, and how AI use affects public authority responsibility. The ombudsman raised questions about how fundamental rights, good governance, and official accountability are secured when AI performs government functions. The municipality subsequently clarified that its primary goal was not to expand AI use or reduce administration, but to maintain essential public services. Index analysis The case represents a novel application of generative AI to core government decision-making and administrative rule-making. The ombudsman found the case raised questions about how legality oversight and proper procedures can be maintained when AI systems perform official duties. Governance controls The municipality did not disclose that governance controls were in place before deploying AI to decision-making and rule-writing functions. The ombudsman's investigation specifically examined whether controls exist to ensure lawful decision-making and proper handling of administrative tasks.

title: AI-generated fake IDs used to rent e-bikes in Italy
summary: A man and a woman, both foreign nationals, presented themselves at an e-bike rental shop in Val Rendena in Madonna di Campiglio in early September 2026. They rented three high-end e-bikes with a combined commercial value exceeding €15,000, providing foreign identity documents to complete the rental contract which stipulated a two-day return period. The suspects did not return the three e-bikes when due and left no trace. The rental shop owner contacted the carabinieri. Investigation revealed the identity documents used to sign the rental contract were false and had been created using advanced AI software. Reported impact The three high-value e-bikes, worth over €15,000 in total, were not recovered. The suspects had already left Italy on the day the e-bikes were due to be returned. Index analysis Carabinieri from Madonna di Campiglio and Polizia Locale di Pinzolo analysed surveillance footage from the area and identified the SUV used by the suspects. The vehicle's foreign registration plate was deliberately concealed by a roof rack. Officers reconstructed the full registration number from the footage. Following the vehicle's movements, investigators located the hotel where the couple had stayed in Pinzolo, enabling them to establish the suspects' true identities.

title: Biologist alleges Claude AI used unpublished research in enzyme discovery
summary: Biologist Mario Rodriguez Mestre from Copenhagen University alleges that Anthropic's Claude AI model may have used unpublished research from his four-year study of enzyme systems (ARTs) to make a recent enzyme discovery that Anthropic announced. Mestre states his team has regularly used Anthropic's AI models in their research for the past three years and provided important findings about the enzyme to Anthropic during that process. The core question, according to Mestre, is whether Claude reached its conclusion through independent reasoning or was partially directed by his team's earlier work. Mestre expressed concern that information from his research could be used in training future versions of the model. Anthropic stated it is not aware of any prior published studies describing the ARTs system and that Claude was not trained on user input, with its molecular biology team lacking access to such records. Reported impact The allegation has raised broader questions about how much autonomous authority should be granted to AI systems in biotechnological research.

title: AI-generated image of Black boy in trash in Brazilian school material
summary: A recycling activity titled 'A Missão dos Guardiões da Terra' distributed to third-grade students in Itapecerica da Serra included an AI-generated illustration depicting a Black boy inside a recycling trash bin. The material was officially distributed by the municipal prefecture as part of a bimonthly assessment and included over 25 pages. Reported impact Parents and educators expressed indignation over the image and questioned the review and approval criteria used before the content reached classrooms. The representation raised concerns about the message conveyed to students regarding the dignity and value of Black children in educational materials. Index analysis The use of an AI tool to generate the illustration did not eliminate human responsibility for selecting, reviewing and approving the material before classroom distribution. Governance controls The Prefeitura de Itapecerica da Serra formally apologized to the children, families and school community and announced a formal investigation into the illustration. The investigation was to examine the stages of development and review of the activity, including records and professionals involved, with potential administrative and disciplinary measures if irregularities were found.

title: Japanese voice actor sues TikTok over AI voice cloning
summary: Kenjiro Tsuda, a voice actor known for roles in Jujutsu Kaisen and Yu-Gi-Oh!, filed a lawsuit against TikTok over videos featuring an AI-generated clone of his voice. An anonymous TikTok account posted videos with images resembling a Jujutsu Kaisen character and narration that Tsuda claims is an artificial imitation of his distinctive baritone. The account accumulated over 200,000 subscribers and reportedly generated upwards of 500,000 yen in monthly revenue. Reported impact Tsuda demands that TikTok remove the videos and argues that the account gained popularity primarily because its content was narrated by his recognizable voice. Tsuda's legal team contends this infringes his publicity rights—the ability to control and profit from aspects of his identity. The Japan Actors Union expressed concern that the animation industry could be harmed if similar voice-cloning practices continue unchecked. Index analysis TikTok argues in court records that the voice is a generic male voice and that any similarity to Tsuda's is subjective. The platform claims it is not responsible for the content posted by the anonymous account user. Governance controls The Japan Actors Union launched a campaign called "No More" against using generative AI to mimic performers without permission, signaling industry-wide concern about voice-cloning practices.

title: AI-generated deepfakes disrupt elections and businesses with limited defenses
summary: Deepfakes are appearing as paid advertising ahead of the Victorian state election in Australia, depicting events that never occurred such as a machete attack at a petrol station, a woman giving birth on a roadside, and floodwater on parliament steps. A meta-analysis of 19 studies covering more than 24,000 people found that deepfakes appear as persuasive as authentic footage and conventional misinformation. A survey of 250 U.S. security leaders found 74% have encountered or suspect a deepfake attack in the past year, yet only 10% have purpose-built tools to defend against them. Reported impact Research found that deepfakes are associated with lower trust in news and democratic institutions and can contribute to the 'liar's dividend,' where genuine content is dismissed as inauthentic. Nearly half of the participants in one experiment incorrectly labeled a real political video as fake or were unsure of its authenticity. Among affected enterprises, nearly half reported costs of $500,000 or more from deepfake attacks, including direct losses, remediation and staff time. One in four reported costs of $1 million or more from a single incident, and 49% experienced follow-on cyberattacks such as ransomware. Index analysis Commercial and open-source AI tools now enable anyone to produce deepfakes without specialist technical expertise, and quality is improving, making detection harder. An experiment with 411 Australians found roughly 75% could correctly identify deepfakes regardless of quality, but around one in four could not confidently identify them or authentic content. Governance controls 93% of surveyed security leaders expressed concern their organizations are not prepared for deepfake attacks, yet research suggests this concern has not translated into boardroom urgency to implement defenses.

title: AI Digital Humans Pose as Medical Experts to Advertise Products in China
summary: An AI short-drama production company released an advertisement featuring an AI digital human claiming in first person: 'I wore contact lenses for a day and they were very comfortable,' with product links included. Contact lenses in China are regulated as Class III medical devices, the same risk level as pacemakers, artificial joints, and stents. CCTV reporters found that low-cost mobile applications can generate AI digital human endorsement videos in minutes. Users upload a single photo, select 'product promotion video,' and receive an 8-second AI video in a few minutes for weekly fees as low as 48 yuan. The apps allow users to specify that the digital human wear medical worker clothing. Multiple platforms display AI digital humans posed as 'medical workers' and 'domain experts' promoting eye disease treatments, hair-loss products, and health supplements. Promotional videos frequently used exaggerated claims like 'cure at the root' and displayed fake scientific experiments. Reported impact Experts warned that AI digital humans impersonating medical professionals create a 'negative trust amplifier' that lowers the barrier to impersonation and misleads consumers unfamiliar with AI into believing they are receiving legitimate medical advice. One expert cautioned that patients with cardiovascular disease are at particular risk, as they may trust claims about 'dissolving arterial plaque' and stop taking prescribed medications, returning themselves to high-risk status. Index analysis China's Advertising Law explicitly prohibits medical, pharmaceutical, and medical device advertisements from using endorsers for recommendations or testimonies. Legal experts noted that AI digital humans can only serve as endorsers if backed by a real person responsible for their statements, and that 'native' AI digital humans with no real person behind them cannot legally endorse products due to lack of genuine experience. The generation software used to create these videos contains no algorithmic restrictions preventing the creation of medical worker endorsements, despite the legal prohibitions. Governance controls Chinese legal experts emphasized that digital humans claiming personal experiences unique to real humans—such as 'this food tastes great' or 'contact lenses were comfortable'—may constitute false advertising if no real person substantiates the claim.

title: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse AI from making purchases without authorization
summary: Amazon blocked access to Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, from its e-commerce platform after determining the system could perform purchases and access account information without authorization. According to Amazon, Meta never requested permission for Muse to use its website. Amazon states that Muse does not identify itself while browsing and can access account pages and order history when the user requests it. The issue centers on how Meta designed the agent. Muse connects to services with public APIs using user-provided credentials, and uses a browser to access services without APIs, functioning similarly to how a person would. Amazon claims Muse captures and stores credentials provided by users, while Meta maintains the credentials are stored securely and Muse cannot view passwords or payment methods. Reported impact Amazon placed a message warning users that access by an unauthorized AI agent violated the platform's terms of use beginning Sunday evening. Amazon states that unrestricted access by Muse poses risks related to privacy, security, and handling of confidential information. Index analysis The conflict extends beyond technical security concerns. An AI that makes purchases on behalf of users controls which products it researches, compares, and which stores it visits, potentially displacing part of the control that platforms like Amazon exercise over search results, recommendations, and advertising. Governance controls Meta states that Muse operates within a secure virtual machine and has its own browser. The system consults the user before performing sensitive actions such as sending emails or making purchases, and an independent agent called Sentinel must approve everything Muse sends.

title: Unauthorized Face Scraping for AI Short Dramas Violates Rights in China
summary: In China's rapidly expanding AI short drama market, a grey market has emerged where people's facial images are scraped from social media platforms without consent, fused using AI tools, and sold as virtual character assets to drama producers. Vendors openly advertise face fusion packages on second-hand platforms for as low as 19.8 yuan (approximately $2.80 USD), containing nearly 500 facial asset variations. The source material for these AI-generated faces comes from screenshots of ordinary social media users, particularly women, extracted from video platforms and overseas social media by searching keywords like 'Chinese people,' 'beauty,' and 'fashion.' Vendors acknowledge the process completely bypasses authorization requirements, with per-image production costs estimated at only 0.02–0.04 yuan. Reported impact Female social media users have had their photographs publicly stolen and resold without consent or compensation. Some AI short dramas have been shut down after using poorly disguised stolen likenesses or distorting the faces of ordinary people in negative portrayals. Actors in the legitimate short drama industry face employment displacement and unauthorized use of their likenesses, with some cases already ruled as copyright infringement when AI characters too closely resembled well-known performers. Index analysis The practice violates China's Civil Code provisions requiring consent before creating, publicizing, or using someone's likeness, and prohibits fabricating likenesses using information technology. Unauthorized large-scale collection and provision of facial data—a sensitive personal information category—may trigger criminal liability under laws protecting citizen privacy. The incident reflects inadequate governance and oversight in the AI-generated content sector, where facial recognition and synthesis technology is deployed at scale without adequate consent mechanisms or content moderation systems. Governance controls A South China Media reporter deleted collected materials and reported incidents to platforms and relevant authorities. Some short dramas using stolen or defamatory AI faces have been removed from circulation.

title: Russia uses AI-generated ads on Meta and Google to recruit foreign fighters for Ukraine war
summary: Code for Africa, an African nonprofit network of digital democracy labs, documented a Russian online recruitment operation targeting young men from Africa, Asia, and Belarus for the war in Ukraine. Researchers identified 89 websites, 7 social media accounts including on Facebook, and 39 messenger accounts or channels used in the operation. The operation used AI-generated images in advertisements, including one showing AI-generated images of Black men in military uniforms placed on a Facebook page based in Germany and labeled as a 'global casting' for a film project with shooting in 2025. Another advertisement sponsored by 'IRC Russian Bear' offered $15,000 immediately upon contract signing and $3,000 monthly salary. Reported impact The recruitment targeted unemployed or underemployed young men in poor labor markets with salary offers significantly higher than they could earn in their home countries. Advertisements rarely mentioned war, instead presenting opportunities in construction, security, film roles, or Russian visa assistance. Meta removed over 300 advertising campaigns linked to the recruiters according to Code for Africa director Justin Arensztein. Google's EMEA spokesman Alex McPhillips disputed claims that most referenced sites used Google ads and said the company was 'actively reviewing' the report. Index analysis The investigation documents a large-scale online recruitment operation using tools from major Western technology platforms. New websites and pages appeared daily, and many sites did not hide their activity despite remaining online, revealing gaps in platform moderation. Governance controls Meta removed over 300 advertising campaigns linked to the recruiters. Google stated it was 'actively reviewing' Code for Africa's report but disputed that most referenced sites used its advertising platform.

title: AI-Generated News Broadcast Raises Labor Concerns in Argentina
summary: El Primer Feca, a news broadcast launched in early September 2026 on Instagram and X by technology educator Santiago Siri, is entirely generated by artificial intelligence, from news content to presenter avatars. The system uses ChatGPT and Openclaw to automatically write news articles and generate videos of AI-created journalists presenting the news, with avatars including presenter Clara Ferrer and specialist correspondents covering economy, sports, technology, geopolitics, entertainment and weather. Reported impact Argentine media professionals have expressed concerns that the AI-generated broadcast threatens employment in journalism and constitutes content scraping from existing news sources. Siri has responded by calling for less obscurantism regarding the technology. Index analysis The broadcast presents real news gathered by AI agents, though the articles note occasional diction errors in the AI-generated videos.

title: Microsoft and partners dismantle EvilTokens AI-powered phishing platform
summary: EvilTokens was a phishing-as-a-service platform launched on Telegram in mid-February 2026 that sold do-it-yourself phishing kits for between $100 and $300 per month. The kit included an AI-powered analyst that mapped trusted relationships, identified who controlled payments, and flagged where fraud was most likely to succeed. The platform exploited Microsoft's device authorization grant flow by directing victims to real Microsoft pages and asking them to enter a device code generated by attackers, enabling attackers to obtain persistent OAuth tokens that granted full access to Microsoft 365 accounts and bypassed multi-factor authentication. The operation compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft 365 inboxes across over 10,000 organizations globally, with independent analysis finding 8,708 accounts spanning 6,585 domains across 79 countries. On September 22, 2026, Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit announced it had dismantled the core infrastructure behind EvilTokens in coordination with Coinbase, Health-ISAC, SpyCloud, and local law enforcement. Two UK administrators, aged 32 and 38, were arrested and subsequently released on bail while investigations continue. Reported impact The platform defrauded businesses ranging from real estate firms to banks to healthcare providers of millions of dollars through phishing emails. Device-code phishing attacks increased by 1,380% in the period following the platform's launch. Index analysis The EvilTokens AI system represented a notable evolution in phishing campaigns by automatically analyzing email accounts to identify the most likely fraud targets, moving beyond traditional 'spray and pray' approaches. The platform's low technical barrier to entry and subscription model enabled threat actors to operate phishing attacks at industrial scale. Governance controls Microsoft and its partners were able to dismantle the platform's infrastructure and arrest the operators, but the investigation revealed that the phishing network had already compromised thousands of organizations before being shut down.

title: Stanford University used AI to alter student photos without consent
summary: Stanford Residential & Dining Enterprises used AI to alter photographs taken for campus advertisements. The original photo, taken at a Lunar New Year party in 2024, showed student Billy Ramirez and other students holding plates of food in a cafeteria setting. In the altered version distributed in promotional materials, Ramirez, a Hispanic male student, was replaced with an AI-generated image of a Black woman. Two other students in the photo were not replaced but had their faces digitally slimmed down. Reported impact Ramirez said he felt "silenced and erased" when he discovered his identity had been changed without his consent. He stated: "Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me." Index analysis Stanford's AI policy explicitly prohibits the use of AI in producing or altering images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. A university spokesperson confirmed that "the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy." Governance controls Stanford removed the altered image and its promotional materials after the violation was discovered. The university announced plans to provide additional staff training and implement proper review procedures for all materials to prevent future violations.

title: Stanford Used Generative AI to Alter Student Photo for Campus Banner
summary: Stanford University's Residential & Dining Enterprises used generative AI to alter a photograph of students taken at the 2024 Lunar New Year Dinner for use in campus promotional banners. The AI replaced the image of Hispanic male student Billy Ramirez with a nonexistent Black woman, while also slimming the faces of two other students (an Asian woman and white man) and changing all three students' clothing to Stanford merchandise. The altered image was displayed on 'Welcome Home' banners at Governor's Corner student housing center and across campus. Ramirez discovered the change when a friend sent him the edited photo and stated that the banners have since been taken down. Reported impact Ramirez said he felt 'silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me.' He initially found the alteration humorous but became upset at the university's willingness to alter his identity without consent or disclosure. The incident sparked national controversy and media attention, with coverage from outlets including The New York Times and San Francisco Chronicle. Ramirez stated he was exhausted by the attention and did not want his legacy at Stanford to be defined by this incident. Index analysis The alteration violated Stanford's AI policy, which explicitly prohibits the use of AI to alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements. University spokesperson Charlene Gage confirmed that both the alteration and lack of disclosure violated university policy. School officials have not reported contacting Ramirez or offering an apology since the incident became public.
